_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have a mutation that leads to MET exon 14 skipping as detected by an FDA-approved test.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-agent, non-randomized, open-label Phase II study
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with metastatic NSCLC whose tumors have a MET exon 14 skipping mutation; Cohort 4 previously treated (one or two prior therapies) and Cohort 5b treatment-naïve
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1 as assessed by Blinded Independent Review Committee (BIRC); key secondary endpoint duration of response (DOR)
pivotal_trials.n: 97 patients with MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC (Cohort 4 N=69; Cohort 5b N=28)
pivotal_trials.result: Cohort 4 (previously treated): ORR 40.6% (95% CI 28.9, 53.1), median DOR 9.72 months (95% CI 5.55, 12.98). Cohort 5b (treatment-naïve): ORR 67.9% (95% CI 47.6, 84.1), median DOR 11.14 months (95% CI 5.55, NE).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): peripheral edema (52%), nausea (44%), fatigue (32%), vomiting (28%), dyspnea (24%), decreased appetite (21%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 51% of patients; ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 4.5% with one fatal case (0.3%).
target_moa: Capmatinib is an orally bioavailable, ATP-competitive kinase inhibitor that targets the MET receptor tyrosine kinase, including the mutated variant produced by MET exon 14 skipping.
companion_dx_detail: FoundationOne CDx (Foundation Medicine) was reviewed contemporaneously as the companion diagnostic to detect MET exon 14 skipping mutations.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to full approval for adult patients with metastatic NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping mutations

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for conversion from accelerated to full approval of Tabrecta tablets for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have a mutation that leads to mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 skipping as detected by an FDA-approved test.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR).

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response [see *Clinical Studies (14)*]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s).

confirmatory_requirement.text: Required confirmatory studies (PMR 3828-1) to confirm and further characterize clinical benefit via a more precise estimation of BIRC-assessed ORR and DOR in treatment-naïve and previously platinum-treated MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC patients.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation granted March 15, 2019 for treatment of NSCLC with MET genomic tumor aberrations.

citations.quote: The FDA granted capmatinib orphan designation for treatment of NSCLC with MET genomic tumor aberrations in March 15, 2019. Because capmatinib has orphan drug designation for NSCLC it is exempt from the PREA requirements and no pediatric studies have been conducted in NSCLC. For approved drugs or biological products for which orphan designation has been granted are exempt from the PREA section 505B

summary.text: NDA 213591 received a Priority review and was granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 based on ORR and DOR from the single-arm Study A2201 (GEOMETRY mono-1), with a required post-marketing confirmatory study; capmatinib also held orphan drug designation for NSCLC with MET genomic tumor aberrations.
